notes.text: This undated handwritten leaf bears a heavy upper 4), a lower circled 4 with a separate point, and thin lower-left foliation 17. The body defines compatibility of a partie-bord with a family through a cylindrical neighbourhood, then strict compatibility of a conic neighbourhood using the complementary X* and its induced family. It begins definitions of equisingularity via locally trivial fibrations. These are source-content descriptions, not proof claims. The final sentence stops after the locally doubtful même and is not completed.

Insertion and cancellation scope were read separately from word identity. B de X has one curved attachment and is followed by one live est; H’s extra struck est is not independently on the page. The au sens cylindrique insertion attaches after compatible, and its doubtful closing arc meets the main-line y. strict has two underlines; strictement has one underline plus a distinct attachment leader, fully captured in completing crop P17. The long elle ... et si insertion includes its final et si. The main line physically divides seule-/ment. The upper marginal note has no secure terminal stop; no quote marks were supplied.

The inserted formula is preserved literally as X_i\cap T=\mathbf I.X_i\cap\dot T-, including its heavy serif interval symbol, multiplication point, lack of supplied grouping parentheses, and final dash. No operand, union term or missing sign is completed. Main T forms have one roof, not an added bar. This paragraph is a transcription/formula-scope observation, not a verification of the displayed condition.

The lower definition literally says les Y_i sont coniques after introducing a family T_i\subset T. The forked Y has no T roof; H’s T_i is not adopted. The first équisingulier has an independent acute, whereas the second equisingulier has none identifiable. First relation: dotted T, a short upper dash, a longer lower unheaded/bent shaft, and Y; its role remains doubtful. The later dotted-T_i-to-Y relation has a definite two-sided arrowhead. The two relations are not silently made identical.

The large transverse margin is not a container for overlapping upright body text. P10 was made from original [16,855,480,1585], rotated clockwise45 (expanded846×846), then scaled to2600×2600. Inverse mapping sends the large cross/return after the final marginal Y to approximately original x273–402,y1296–1309, centred at (325,1309): the main-line X_i already transcribed in P08. The lower long downward stroke maps from about (293,1431) to (406,1421): the main-line ment continuation. A rotated cross near the earlier cancelled equality maps to (338,1015), also upright-body X-star ink. These are excluded from the margin. In contrast, the short dash before its live zero-image equality maps to (51,1472) and is genuinely marginal. The final marginal formula has an overbar above its right side, not a source underline.

Targeted conditional check of the marginal i.e.: interpret dot X_i as X_i\cap dot T, the zero action as the retraction to Y, and the final overbar as closure in X of X_i\setminus(X_i\cap Y). For a closed conic-compatible X_i, equality 0.dot X_i=X_i\cap Y implies the density formula: for each y in the intersection choose a boundary point b with 0.b=y; the positive points t.b approach y as t tends to zero and remain outside Y. Points already outside Y need no approximation. Closedness then gives X_i=cl_X(X_i\setminus Y). Conversely, density gives only density of the zero-image in X_i\cap Y under the conic-ray interpretation: a continuous zero retraction sends approximating positive rays to 0.dot X_i. Continuity does not make that image closed or surjective. This is a limited proof check of the two conditions, not a proof of all source definitions.

The converse in the marginal i.e. is refuted by the following explicit example, proposed by root and independently checked here. Put A=(0,1], Y=[0,1], f:A\to Y the inclusion, and let X be the quotient of Y disjoint-union (A×[0,2]) identifying (a,0) with f(a). Let T be Y together with the images of A×[0,1], dot T=A×{1}, use the usual scalar action on heights in T, and take X_i=X (closed). Y and T are closed; T contains the open neighbourhood consisting of Y and heights<1. Its exterior X* is A×[1,2], so dot T has the explicit product collar there. Compatibility with X_i=X is automatic. If a stronger strictness formulation requires shrinking by a homeomorphism, the increasing piecewise-linear height map h_lambda(t)=lambda*t on [0,1] and h_lambda(t)=lambda+(2-lambda)*(t-1) on [1,2] fixes0,2 and sends1 to lambda; it descends to the quotient fixing Y and sends T to lambda T. The positive part X\setminus Y is dense: every neighbourhood of y in Y has an open Y portion meeting A; if a is in that intersection, openness in the cylinder gives points (a,t) with t>0 in the neighbourhood. Thus X_i=cl_X(X_i\setminus Y)=X. However 0.dot X_i=f(A)=(0,1] is a proper subset of X_i\cap Y=[0,1]. Therefore the displayed density condition does not in general imply the zero-image equality, even with the explicit strict ambient collar. No source formula has been corrected.

The counterexample in N07 addresses the marginal i.e. between zero-image equality and density. The main inserted expression has the literal unfinished-looking ending X_i\cap T=I.X_i\cap dot T-. If that separate expression is completed/interpreted as the exact stronger hypothesis X_i\cap T=I·(X_i\cap dot T), then, under the usual conic-ray interpretation, intersecting with Y already imposes X_i\cap Y=0.dot X_i. N07 does not satisfy that extra equality, and is not claimed to refute a definition that includes it. The unclear terminal dash and the missing grouping are preserved rather than resolved by this diagnostic.

Independent audit: root personally inspected all 24 nonidentical boxes, the full slanted-margin crops and a wider native-orientation context. Six boxes were revised. The raised et underline is restored; the cancelled equality now prefers plain right-hand X_i; the lower adjective now prefers live strict with its earlier deletion reading retained as an alternative. Other new alternatives retain the earlier preferred text and do not create primary C corrections. Fixed first/second readings remain unchanged.

Checked density, proper zero image, closed X_i, ambient collar and the descended piecewise-linear shrinking homeomorphism.
